question: Does replacing the system-wide pswpout abort with a run-cgroup memory.swap.current delta prevent unrelated swap activity from invalidating the holdout while preserving protection against swap charged to the inference worker?
hypothesis: The global /proc/vmstat pswpout counter is not attributable to the test cgroup. A run-cgroup memory.swap.current delta is attributable and should remain a safety signal; global pswpout remains recorded for host telemetry only.

planned_change.record: run-cgroup memory.swap.current bytes, baseline, delta, and system-wide pswpin/pswpout deltas
planned_change.abort_rule: Abort only when run-cgroup memory.swap.current grows by more than 4 MiB; retain existing MemAvailable and sustained global/run-cgroup PSI aborts

cpu_only_regressions: A >4 MiB global pswpout delta with abundant MemAvailable, low PSI, and no run-cgroup swap delta is recorded but does not abort.
A >4 MiB run-cgroup memory.swap.current delta aborts.
MemAvailable below 20 GiB and sustained severe global/run-cgroup PSI still abort.
acceptance: All Q35 CPU-only regression tests pass; py_compile passes; no GPU or inference server is started. Only after this diagnosis is documented may a new attempt be preregistered and preflighted.
non_goals: do not change model, quantization, requested context, sampling, or worker memory budget
do not claim a quality result from attempt 06
